title: Where Shots was from, and Bill Johnson on banjo
summary: Brief exchanges about Shots's origins and Bill Johnson, who went on tour with the Creole band; Williams was never in Chicago or New York.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: A young man, not an old man, he was a young man, you know. He was a children. What about Shots, where was he from? Third Ward. Oh, the Third Ward. Shots was born in the Third Ward too, but not where I ran.
I don't know, but he's from the Third Ward.
How long did you know him?
Shots, I knew him a pretty good while. But I really didn't know him well until he started playing music, you see. Yeah. Mm-hmm.
Did you know Stink's brother Bill Johnson? No, I didn't know him.
No, I didn't know him. No, I didn't never see him. He played banjo and face.
Yeah, that's right. What was his name?
Bill Johnson. Bill Johnson. He must have been out in Los Angeles, but I was out there, wasn't he?

Yeah, I think he was out there real early. Yeah, he did. No, he went on the road, you see. With a show? They had that Creole band with Kepa, the big ol' little. Yeah, with Kepa, I see, that's from my time.
Yeah, from my time. Yeah, from my time.
And then he went up and played with Joe Oliver. Where, Chicago? In Chicago.
Never been in Chicago in my life. I've traveled all around, never been in Chicago or New York.
